note: Questions from the CBSE Class XII Chemistry board exam 2024, Q.P. code 56/1/1, published by CBSE at cbse.gov.in. Structural formulae are written as names or condensed formulae. Solutions are written for this portal and are not CBSE's official marking scheme.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which one of the following first row transition elements is expected to have the highest third ionization enthalpy?
questions.solution: Mn²⁺ is 3d⁵ (half-filled, extra stable), so removing a third electron needs the most energy.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following compounds will give a ketone on oxidation with chromic anhydride (CrO₃)?
questions.solution: Secondary alcohols (butan-2-ol) are oxidised to ketones.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Two among the three components of DNA are β-D-2-deoxyribose and a heterocyclic base. The third component is :
questions.solution: A nucleotide has a sugar, a base and a phosphate group (from phosphoric acid).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: For an electrolyte undergoing association in a solvent, the van't Hoff factor :
questions.solution: Association reduces the number of particles, so i < 1.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: For the reaction X + 2Y → P, the differential form of the rate law is :
questions.solution: Rate = −d[X]/dt = −½ d[Y]/dt = d[P]/dt, so 2 d[P]/dt = −d[Y]/dt.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The compound which undergoes SN1 reaction most rapidly is :
questions.solution: 3-Bromocyclohexene forms a resonance-stabilised allylic carbocation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Acetic acid reacts with PCl₅ to give :
questions.solution: CH₃COOH + PCl₅ → CH₃COCl + POCl₃ + HCl.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The formation of cyanohydrin from an aldehyde is an example of :
questions.solution: CN⁻ adds to the carbonyl carbon.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: In the Arrhenius equation, when log k is plotted against 1/T, a straight line is obtained whose :
options: slope is A/R and intercept is Eₐ
slope is A and intercept is −Eₐ/R
slope is −Eₐ/RT and intercept is log A
slope is −Eₐ/(2.303R) and intercept is log A
questions.solution: log k = log A − Eₐ/(2.303RT).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The reaction of an alkyl halide with sodium alkoxide forming an ether is known as :
questions.solution: R–X + R′ONa → R–O–R′ + NaX is Williamson synthesis.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The correct order of the ease of dehydration of the following alcohols by the action of conc. H₂SO₄ is :
questions.solution: Ease follows carbocation stability: tertiary > secondary > primary.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which functional groups of glucose interact to form the cyclic hemiacetal leading to the pyranose structure?
options: Aldehyde group and hydroxyl group at C-4
Aldehyde group and hydroxyl group at C-5
Ketone group and hydroxyl group at C-4
Ketone group and hydroxyl group at C-5
questions.solution: The C-5 –OH adds to the C-1 aldehyde, forming a six-membered ring.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Assertion (A): When NaCl is added to water, a depression in freezing point is observed.
Reason (R): NaCl undergoes dissociation in water.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: Any non-volatile solute lowers the freezing point; dissociation only increases the effect, so R does not explain A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Assertion (A): Separation of Zr and Hf is difficult.
Reason (R): Zr and Hf have similar radii due to lanthanoid contraction.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: Lanthanoid contraction makes their radii almost equal, so their properties are very similar.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Assertion (A): The pKₐ of ethanoic acid is lower than that of Cl–CH₂–COOH.
Reason (R): Chlorine shows an electron-withdrawing (−I) effect which increases the acidic character of Cl–CH₂–COOH.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: Chloroacetic acid is stronger, so it has the lower pKₐ; A is false and R is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Assertion (A): Aniline is a stronger base than ammonia.
Reason (R): The unshared electron pair on the nitrogen atom in aniline becomes less available for protonation due to resonance.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: Aniline is weaker than ammonia because of the resonance described in R.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Calculate the potential of an iron electrode in which the concentration of Fe²⁺ ions is 0.01 M. (E°(Fe²⁺/Fe) = −0.45 V at 298 K) [Given : log 10 = 1]

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Define molecularity of a reaction. State any one condition in which a bimolecular reaction may be kinetically of first order.
questions.solution: Molecularity is the number of reacting species (atoms, ions or molecules) that must collide simultaneously in an elementary step. A bimolecular reaction is first order when one reactant is in large excess, e.g. water in the acid hydrolysis of an ester (pseudo first order).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: What happens when D-glucose is treated with the following reagents? (a) HI (b) Conc. HNO₃
questions.solution: (a) On prolonged heating it is reduced to n-hexane. (b) It is oxidised to saccharic acid (glucaric acid), HOOC(CHOH)₄COOH.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Write the structures of the major monohalo products in each of the following reactions : (i) Styrene (C₆H₅CH=CH₂) + HBr (ii) Cyclohexane + Br₂ in UV light
questions.solution: (i) Markovnikov addition gives 1-bromo-1-phenylethane, C₆H₅CH(Br)CH₃. (ii) Free-radical substitution gives bromocyclohexane, C₆H₁₁Br.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Give reasons for the following : (i) Grignard reagent should be prepared under anhydrous conditions. (ii) Alkyl halides give alcohols with aqueous KOH whereas in the presence of alcoholic KOH, alkenes are formed.
questions.solution: (i) Grignard reagents react with water (RMgX + H₂O → RH + Mg(OH)X), so moisture destroys them. (ii) In water, OH⁻ is heavily solvated and acts as a nucleophile (substitution). Alcoholic KOH gives alkoxide ions, strong bases that remove a β-hydrogen (elimination).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Write the chemical equation when : (a) Butan-2-one is treated with Zn(Hg) and conc. HCl. (b) Two molecules of benzaldehyde are treated with conc. NaOH.
questions.solution: (a) Clemmensen reduction: CH₃COCH₂CH₃ → CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₃ (butane). (b) Cannizzaro reaction: 2C₆H₅CHO + NaOH → C₆H₅CH₂OH + C₆H₅COONa.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: When a certain conductivity cell was filled with 0.05 M KCl solution, it had a resistance of 100 ohm at 25 °C. When the same cell was filled with 0.02 M AgNO₃ solution, the resistance was 90 ohm. Calculate the conductivity and molar conductivity of the AgNO₃ solution. (Conductivity of 0.05 M KCl = 1.35 × 10⁻² ohm⁻¹ cm⁻¹)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Initial rate data for 2NO(g) + Br₂(g) → 2NOBr(g): Expt 1: [NO] = 0.05, [Br₂] = 0.05, rate 1.0 × 10⁻³; Expt 2: 0.05, 0.15, 3.0 × 10⁻³; Expt 3: 0.15, 0.05, 9.0 × 10⁻³ (concentrations in mol L⁻¹, rate in mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹). (a) What is the order with respect to NO and Br₂? (b) Calculate the rate constant k. (c) Determine the rate when the concentrations of NO and Br₂ are 0.4 M and 0.2 M respectively.
questions.solution: (a) Tripling [Br₂] triples the rate: first order in Br₂. Tripling [NO] makes it 9 times: second order in NO. Rate = k[NO]²[Br₂]. (b) k = 1.0 × 10⁻³/(0.05² × 0.05) = 8 L² mol⁻² s⁻¹. (c) Rate = 8 × 0.4² × 0.2 = 0.256 mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: (a) Write the formula of potassium tetrahydroxidozincate(II). (b) Arrange in increasing order of conductivity of their solutions : [Cr(NH₃)₅Cl]Cl₂, [Cr(NH₃)₃Cl₃], [Cr(NH₃)₆]Cl₃. (c) Identify the type of isomerism shown by (i) [Co(NH₃)₅NO₂]²⁺ (ii) [Co(en)₃]Cl₃.
questions.solution: (a) K₂[Zn(OH)₄]. (b) [Cr(NH₃)₃Cl₃] (no ions) < [Cr(NH₃)₅Cl]Cl₂ (3 ions) < [Cr(NH₃)₆]Cl₃ (4 ions). (c) (i) Linkage isomerism (–NO₂ / –ONO). (ii) Optical isomerism.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: (a) Which of the following is an allylic halide? (i) CH₃–CH=CH–Br (ii) CH₂=CH–CH(Br)–CH₃ (b) Out of chlorobenzene and 2,4,6-trinitrochlorobenzene, which is more reactive towards nucleophilic substitution and why? (c) Which isomer of C₄H₉Cl has the lowest boiling point?
questions.solution: (a) (ii): the halogen is on the carbon next to the C=C. (i) is a vinylic halide. (b) 2,4,6-Trinitrochlorobenzene: the –NO₂ groups at ortho and para positions withdraw electrons and stabilise the intermediate carbanion. (c) 2-Chloro-2-methylpropane, (CH₃)₃CCl (most branched).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: (a) Write the mechanism of the reaction CH₃CH₂OH —H⁺, 443 K→ CH₂=CH₂. (b) Write the main product in each of the following reactions : (i) CH₃–CH₂–CH=CH₂ with (a) B₂H₆ (b) 3H₂O₂/OH⁻ (ii) Phenol with (a) aq. NaOH (b) CO₂, H⁺
questions.solution: (a) Step 1: protonation of ethanol to CH₃CH₂–OH₂⁺. Step 2: loss of water to give the carbocation CH₃CH₂⁺ (slow). Step 3: loss of H⁺ from the adjacent carbon to give CH₂=CH₂. (b)(i) Hydroboration-oxidation (anti-Markovnikov): butan-1-ol, CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂OH. (ii) Kolbe's reaction: 2-hydroxybenzoic acid (salicylic acid).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Answer any three : (a) What is a peptide linkage? (b) What type of bonds hold a DNA double helix together? (c) Which one of the following is a polysaccharide? Sucrose, Glucose, Starch, Fructose (d) Give one example each of water-soluble and fat-soluble vitamins.
questions.solution: (a) The amide bond –CO–NH– formed between the –COOH of one amino acid and the –NH₂ of another, with loss of water. (b) Hydrogen bonds between complementary base pairs (A–T and G–C). (c) Starch. (d) Water-soluble: vitamin C (or B-group); fat-soluble: vitamin A (or D, E, K).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Compound A (C₆H₁₂O₂) on reduction with LiAlH₄ gives two compounds B and C. B on oxidation with PCC gives D, which upon treatment with dilute NaOH and subsequent heating gives E. E on catalytic hydrogenation gives C. D is oxidised further to give F, a monobasic acid (molecular weight 60). Identify A, B, C, D, E and F.
questions.solution: F (M = 60) is acetic acid, so D = ethanal and B = ethanol. Aldol condensation of ethanal gives E = but-2-enal, which on full hydrogenation gives C = butan-1-ol. So A is the ester butyl ethanoate, CH₃COOCH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃ (C₆H₁₂O₂).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Batteries and fuel cells are useful forms of galvanic cell. A practical battery should be light and compact, and its voltage should not vary appreciably during use. There are two main types: primary batteries, in which the reaction occurs only once and the battery cannot be reused, and secondary batteries, which are rechargeable. Thermal power generation is inefficient and polluting, so galvanic cells have been designed that convert the energy of combustion of fuels directly into electrical energy; these are fuel cells. One such fuel cell was used in the Apollo space programme.

How do primary batteries differ from secondary batteries?
questions.solution: Primary batteries cannot be recharged once used (e.g. dry cell); secondary batteries can be recharged by passing current in the reverse direction (e.g. lead storage battery).

questions.solution: The overall reaction, Zn(Hg) + HgO → ZnO + Hg, involves no ions in solution whose concentration changes.

Write the reactions involved in the recharging of the lead storage battery.
questions.solution: At one electrode: PbSO₄ + 2e⁻ → Pb + SO₄²⁻. At the other: PbSO₄ + 2H₂O → PbO₂ + SO₄²⁻ + 4H⁺ + 2e⁻. Overall: 2PbSO₄ + 2H₂O → Pb + PbO₂ + 2H₂SO₄.

Write two advantages of fuel cells over other galvanic cells.
questions.solution: They run continuously as long as fuel is supplied; they are highly efficient (about 70%); they cause little pollution (H₂–O₂ cells give only water).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Valence bond theory (VBT) explains the formation, magnetic behaviour and geometrical shapes of coordination compounds, whereas crystal field theory (CFT) is based on the effect of the crystal fields of the ligands (taken as point charges) on the degeneracy of the d-orbital energies of the central metal atom or ion. The splitting of the d-orbitals gives different electronic arrangements in strong and weak crystal fields. CFT attributes the colour of coordination compounds to d–d transitions. Coordination compounds have extensive applications in metallurgy and in analytical and medicinal chemistry.

What is crystal field splitting energy?
questions.solution: The energy difference between the two sets of d-orbitals (e.g. t₂g and e_g in an octahedral field) produced by the ligand field, written Δo for octahedral complexes.

The splitting of the d-orbitals gives different electronic arrangements in strong and weak crystal fields. CFT attributes the colour of coordination compounds to d–d transitions. Give the reason for the violet colour of the complex [Ti(H₂O)₆]³⁺ on the basis of crystal field theory.
questions.solution: Ti³⁺ is 3d¹ (t₂g¹). The electron absorbs green-yellow light to jump to the e_g level (d–d transition), and the complementary colour, violet, is seen.

[Cr(NH₃)₆]³⁺ is paramagnetic while [Ni(CN)₄]²⁻ is diamagnetic. Explain why. [Atomic No. : Cr = 24, Ni = 28]
questions.solution: Cr³⁺ is 3d³; with d²sp³ hybridisation the three d electrons stay unpaired in t₂g, so it is paramagnetic. Ni²⁺ is 3d⁸; strong-field CN⁻ pairs the electrons, giving dsp² square planar with no unpaired electrons, so it is diamagnetic.

The splitting of the d-orbitals gives different electronic arrangements in strong and weak crystal fields. CFT attributes the colour of coordination compounds to d–d transitions. Coordination compounds have extensive applications in metallurgy and in analytical and medicinal chemistry.

Explain why [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻ is an inner orbital complex whereas [Fe(H₂O)₆]³⁺ is an outer orbital complex. [Atomic No. : Fe = 26]
questions.solution: Fe³⁺ is 3d⁵. Strong-field CN⁻ pairs the electrons, freeing two inner 3d orbitals for d²sp³ hybridisation (inner orbital). Weak-field H₂O cannot pair them, so the outer 4d orbitals are used (sp³d², outer orbital).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: (i) At the same temperature, CO₂ gas is more soluble in water than O₂ gas. Which one of them will have the higher value of K_H and why? (ii) How does the size of blood cells change when placed in an aqueous solution containing more than 0.9% (mass/volume) sodium chloride? (iii) A 1 molal aqueous solution of an electrolyte A₂B₃ is 60% ionised. Calculate the boiling point of the solution. (K_b for H₂O = 0.52 K kg mol⁻¹)
questions.solution: (i) O₂: by Henry's law p = K_H x, so a less soluble gas has a higher K_H. (ii) The solution is hypertonic, so water leaves the cells and they shrink. (iii) A₂B₃ gives 5 ions: i = 1 + α(5 − 1) = 1 + 0.6 × 4 = 3.4. ΔT_b = iK_b m = 3.4 × 0.52 × 1 ≈ 1.77 K. Boiling point ≈ 101.77 °C (374.92 K).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: (i) The vapour pressures of A and B at 25 °C are 75 mm Hg and 25 mm Hg respectively. If A and B are mixed so that the mole fraction of A in the mixture is 0.4, calculate the mole fraction of B in the vapour phase. (ii) Define colligative property. Which colligative property is preferred for the molar mass determination of macromolecules? (iii) Why are equimolar solutions of sodium chloride and glucose not isotonic?
questions.solution: (i) p_A = 75 × 0.4 = 30, p_B = 25 × 0.6 = 15, total 45 mm Hg. y_B = 15/45 = 1/3 ≈ 0.33. (ii) A property that depends only on the number of solute particles, not their nature (e.g. relative lowering of vapour pressure, osmotic pressure). Osmotic pressure is preferred for macromolecules. (iii) NaCl dissociates into two ions (i ≈ 2) while glucose does not (i = 1), so their osmotic pressures differ.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Answer any five : (a) N,N-diethylbenzenesulphonamide is insoluble in alkali. Give reason. (b) Aniline does not undergo Friedel-Crafts reaction. Why? (c) Write a simple chemical test to distinguish between methylamine and aniline. (d) Write the chemical reaction involved in Gabriel phthalimide synthesis. (e) How will you convert aniline to p-bromoaniline? (f) Complete: benzenediazonium chloride with (i) HBF₄ (ii) NaNO₂/Cu, heat. (g) Write the structures of A and B: benzoic acid —NH₃, heat→ A —Br₂ + NaOH→ B.
questions.solution: (a) It has no hydrogen on the nitrogen, so it is not acidic. (b) Aniline (a Lewis base) forms a salt with the AlCl₃ catalyst; the positive N deactivates the ring. (c) Azo-dye test: aniline, diazotised at 0–5 °C and added to alkaline β-naphthol, gives an orange dye; methylamine does not (it gives N₂ gas). (Carbylamine works for both, so it does not distinguish them.) (d) Phthalimide + KOH → potassium phthalimide; + R–X → N-alkylphthalimide; hydrolysis with NaOH → R–NH₂ + sodium phthalate. (e) Acetylate (acetic anhydride) to acetanilide, brominate (Br₂ in acetic acid) to p-bromoacetanilide, then hydrolyse to p-bromoaniline. (f) C₆H₅N₂⁺BF₄⁻ (fluoroborate), then nitrobenzene, C₆H₅NO₂. (g) A = benzamide, C₆H₅CONH₂; B = aniline, C₆H₅NH₂ (Hofmann bromamide).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: (i) Account for the following : (1) The melting and boiling points of Zn, Cd and Hg are low. (2) Of the d⁴ species, Cr²⁺ is strongly reducing while Mn³⁺ is strongly oxidising. (3) The E° value of Cu²⁺/Cu is +0.34 V. (ii) Complete and balance : (1) KMnO₄ —heat→ (2) Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 6I⁻ + 14H⁺ →
questions.solution: (i)(1) Their d-orbitals are completely filled (d¹⁰), so no d electrons take part in metallic bonding and the bonding is weak. (2) Cr²⁺ → Cr³⁺ gives the stable t₂g³ configuration; Mn³⁺ → Mn²⁺ gives the stable half-filled d⁵ configuration. (3) Copper's high enthalpy of atomisation and ionisation enthalpies are not compensated by its hydration enthalpy, so Cu does not easily form Cu²⁺(aq). (ii)(1) 2KMnO₄ → K₂MnO₄ + MnO₂ + O₂. (2) Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 6I⁻ + 14H⁺ → 2Cr³⁺ + 3I₂ + 7H₂O.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: (i) Out of Cu₂Cl₂ and CuCl₂, which is more stable in aqueous solution and why? (ii) Write the general electronic configuration of f-block elements. (iii) Predict which of Sc³⁺, Fe³⁺ and Zn²⁺ will be coloured in aqueous solution and why. (iv) How can you obtain potassium dichromate from sodium chromate? (v) Why do transition metals and their compounds show catalytic activity?
questions.solution: (i) CuCl₂: Cu²⁺(aq) has a much more negative hydration enthalpy, which outweighs the second ionisation enthalpy; Cu⁺ disproportionates in water. (ii) (n − 2)f¹⁻¹⁴ (n − 1)d⁰⁻¹ ns². (iii) Fe³⁺ (3d⁵, unpaired electrons, d–d transitions) is coloured; Sc³⁺ (3d⁰) and Zn²⁺ (3d¹⁰) are colourless. (iv) Acidify: 2Na₂CrO₄ + 2H⁺ → Na₂Cr₂O₇ + 2Na⁺ + H₂O, then add KCl: Na₂Cr₂O₇ + 2KCl → K₂Cr₂O₇ + 2NaCl (K₂Cr₂O₇ crystallises out). (v) Variable oxidation states, the ability to form unstable intermediates, and a large surface for adsorption of reactants.
